CANDIDATE bd-01M15ZMJC274ABA13QAMQ7XKYJ: 59f8fd0 on branch m1/external-mass, parent current main. Two files: align/signature.scala and a new align/SignatureSuite.scala. Your finding, and it is the align sibling of the interview one exactly as you said.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, and why I chose the structural option over the threshold one. You offered either "exclude unranked and report it beside" or "abstain above a stated threshold". I took the first, and made the pairing STRUCTURAL rather than documentary: externalMass no longer returns a Double at all. It returns ExternalMassReport(attributed, unranked), and there is deliberately NO accessor that hands back the sum. A caller cannot quote the external mass without carrying the caveat, because the sum does not exist as a number anywhere in the API - anyone who genuinely wants it must write attributed + unranked at their own call site, where a reviewer can see them doing it. rankedMass = 1 - unranked states the coverage of the attributed figure.

A threshold would have needed a magic constant and would still have handed back one number below it. This way there is no number to misquote at any threshold.

I did NOT renormalize the remaining five terms, per your estimand guard and the scout's argument on the interview fix - that trades one bias for its mirror.

Also confirmed before changing the shape: RecallSignature.externalMass has NO callers anywhere in the repository's source. It is a public convenience accessor, so this is a pure API improvement with no migration.

THE TRIPWIRE, AND A CAVEAT I OWE YOU ABOUT IT. The guard against someone re-adding the sum is a compile-time check (scala.compiletime.testing.typeChecks) asserting that ExternalMassReport(...).total does not compile, with positive controls asserting that .attributed and .unranked do. That is cross-platform, unlike the reflection version I wrote first, which broke the Scala.js link - align is cross-built and java.lang.reflect does not exist there.

But it has a limitation I found by mutation and have written into the test rather than hidden: A COMPILE-TIME CHECK ONLY RE-EVALUATES WHEN ITS OWN FILE IS RECOMPILED. My first two mutation runs REPORTED PASS with `total` present, which looked like the tripwire failing to fire. It was stale compilation - I had touched the test file, and sbt tracks content, not mtime, so the macro result was cached from the previous build. Changing the test's content made it recompile and it failed correctly, with the probe printing typeChecks(total) = true. So: it works on a clean build and in CI, and it can be silently stale in an incremental dev loop. Worth knowing before anyone else writes one of these.

That is the second time tonight a mutation "survived" for a reason that had nothing to do with the code - the first was a mutant that did not compile. Both times the tell was the same: a result that was too clean given what I had just broken. I would add that to the board's mutation practice as a rule of thumb - when a mutant survives, verify the mutant actually took effect before believing the test is weak.

EVIDENCE at 59f8fd0, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 143/143, alignJS 143/143 (was 138; five new), lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, embedBench 42/42, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.

Queue from me: m1/cost-blend 60cf041 and m1/route 866e493 both landed; m1/route also carries 638294f (false-gating abstention, pending) and this is m1/external-mass 59f8fd0.
